items.prompt: In the expense tracker, addExpense receives the amount text "12.300". What does the manager do with it?
items.answer: Accepts it and stores 12.30, as dropping a trailing zero needs no rounding
distractors: Rejects it with "Amount must use at most 2 decimal places." for the third digit
Accepts it and stores 12.300, as BigDecimal keeps the scale it was parsed with
Rounds it half-up to 12.30 and prints a warning that a digit was discarded
items.explanation: parseAmount calls setScale(2, RoundingMode.UNNECESSARY); 12.300 -> 12.30 changes no value, so it succeeds. 1.001 would throw and become the precision message.

items.prompt: In the delivered code a user types 1e2 as the amount in menu option 1. What does menu 2 then show for that expense?
items.answer: An amount of $100.00, because new BigDecimal reads scientific notation
distractors: No expense: the add fails with "Amount must be a valid number." for the e
An amount of $1.00, as parsing stops at the first character that is not a digit
No expense: the add fails since 1e2 has no decimal point to scale to two places
items.explanation: parseAmount passes the trimmed text straight to new BigDecimal(value), which accepts exponent notation (and a leading sign); setScale(2) then gives 100.00. Verified by running addExpense("x","1e2",...).

items.prompt: Ids 1 and 2 exist. The user deletes #2, chooses 7 to save and exit, restarts the app and adds an expense. Which id does it get?
items.answer: #2, as nextId is rebuilt from the highest id still present in the file
distractors: #3, as the next-id counter is written to the file header and reloaded
#3, because deleted ids go on a tombstone list that blocks their reuse
#1, since a restart resets nextId to its initial value of one
items.explanation: loadExpenses sets nextId = highestId + 1 from the loaded records; no counter is persisted. Within one session the id would be 3, but after a restart the deleted 2 is reissued.

items.prompt: The app starts on a data file whose third line has the amount "thirty". What does the delivered CLI do?
items.answer: Prints the load error, skips the menu and the save, then exits with status 0
distractors: Skips line 3, opens the menu with one expense, and rewrites the file on exit
Refuses to start and returns exit code 1, so a calling script sees the failure
Opens the menu with an empty list, then overwrites the file when you choose 7
items.explanation: load throws IOException for the bad record; run returns early at "if (!loadExpenses()) return;", before the try/finally that saves, and main ends normally, so the process exits 0.

items.prompt: Before the worked change, an expense saved with an empty note vanished on the next load. What made the loader drop it?
items.answer: line.trim() removed the trailing tab, so the parser saw five fields
distractors: toLine left out the note column when it was blank, so five fields were saved
unescape turned the empty note into null, and the constructor refused null
The comment check matched the empty field and skipped the whole line
items.explanation: The saved line ends with a tab that introduces the empty sixth field. Trimming the whole line removed it, the parser rejected a five-field record, and the old catch carried on. The fix parses the original line.

items.prompt: updateExpense(1, "Bus", "2.50", "Travel", "2026-02-30", "changed") runs against a stored Lunch at 12.30. What is stored afterwards?
items.answer: Lunch at 12.30 with its old note, as the call throws before expenses.set
distractors: Bus at 2.50 with the old date, since only the date field failed to validate
Bus at 2.50 on 2026-02-28, as the date parser clamps the day to the month end
No expense #1, as the old entry is removed before the replacement is built
items.explanation: The replacement Expense is built (parseAmount, parseDate) before expenses.set(i, replacement). parseDate throws for Feb 30, so set never runs and the old immutable value stays.

items.prompt: In menu 8 the user types abc where the CLI asks for the expense id. Which line does it print before the menu comes back?
items.answer: Could not update expense: For input string: "abc"
distractors: Could not update expense: Expense id must be positive.
Expense #abc does not exist.
Invalid menu option. Please choose a number from 1 to 9.
items.explanation: Long.parseLong throws NumberFormatException, a subclass of IllegalArgumentException, so the flow catch prints its message after the prefix. The id text is not trimmed, so " 1" fails the same way. Verified by piping 8 then abc into the CLI.

items.prompt: With the default locale set to tr-TR, one expense has category " INCOME   tax " and another "income tax". What does getSpendingByCategory return?
items.answer: One entry, Income Tax, holding both amounts, as case uses Locale.ROOT
distractors: Two entries, as the first label keeps its inner run of spaces after trimming
One entry keyed INCOME TAX, since categories are upper-cased for grouping
One entry spelled with a dotless Turkish i, as case follows the default locale
items.explanation: normalizeCategory trims, splits on whitespace runs, and title-cases each word with Locale.ROOT, so both become "Income Tax" whatever the default locale. The regression test pins this.

items.prompt: The data file holds one valid record. storage.save is then called with two expenses that share id 1. What happens to the file?
items.answer: It stays byte for byte the same, as validation throws before a temp file exists
distractors: It is cut down to the header, as the writer opens the file before validating
It is rewritten with only the first record, and the duplicate is dropped
It is rewritten with both records, and the next load rejects the duplicate
items.explanation: save copies the list and runs it through a fresh ExpenseManager.loadExpenses, which throws on a duplicate id, before createTempFile or any write. The test compares the file bytes after the rejection.

items.prompt: The user puts the line "# my comment" at the top of the data file, starts the app and exits with 7 without changing anything. What is in the file now?
items.answer: The generated header and the records, with the user comment dropped
distractors: The user comment and the records, since an unchanged session is not saved
The user comment above the generated header, as comments are carried over
Nothing new: loading fails on the comment line and startup is refused
items.explanation: load skips any line starting with #, and save always writes its own header plus the records. The finally block saves even when nothing changed, so the comment is lost. Verified with a save/load round trip.

items.prompt: In menu 9 the user enters an existing id and answers the confirmation prompt with YES in capitals. What happens?
items.answer: The expense is removed, since the answer is compared with equalsIgnoreCase
distractors: Deletion is cancelled, as only the exact lowercase word yes confirms it
The prompt repeats until the user answers with yes or no in lowercase
The expense is removed and the file is rewritten before the menu returns
items.explanation: deleteExpenseFlow tests prompt(...).equalsIgnoreCase("yes"), so YES confirms. The removal is in memory; the file is written only by the save in run's finally block.

items.prompt: Piped input completes one add, then ends right after the title of a second add. What does the session write to the file?
items.answer: The completed expense only; the half-entered add never reached the manager
distractors: Nothing; the session ended without the user ever choosing option 7
Both expenses, the second saved with blank fields filled from defaults
Nothing, since the end-of-input exception skips the save in run
items.explanation: scanner.nextLine throws NoSuchElementException at end of input; run catches it, prints "Input ended. Saving completed changes." and the finally block saves. The second add never called addExpense.

items.prompt: After loading one expense with id Long.MAX_VALUE - 1, addExpense is called twice. What happens?
items.answer: The first gets Long.MAX_VALUE; the second throws IllegalStateException
distractors: The first gets Long.MAX_VALUE; the second gets Long.MIN_VALUE after overflow
The first gets Long.MAX_VALUE; the second reuses the lowest free id, 1
Both fail, as Expense rejects any id larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE
items.explanation: After issuing Long.MAX_VALUE, nextId becomes the sentinel 0, and addExpense throws "Expense id space is exhausted." instead of wrapping. The regression test checks both calls.

items.front: Why does the Expense constructor enforce the invariants (positive id, nonblank title and category, two-place positive amount) instead of only the menu code?
items.back: Records enter from two places: the menu and the saved file. Validating only menu input would leave the file-loading path unprotected, so the rule lives where every Expense is built.

items.front: What is a dual write, and what is the fix the course gives for it?
items.back: One logical change that needs two separate durable writes (for example rows in one file and a next-id counter in another). They can fail independently. The fix is to make it one write: same file under one atomic move, or one database transaction.

items.front: save() writes a temp file and moves it over the target with ATOMIC_MOVE. Name three guarantees this does NOT give.
items.back: No cross-process lock (two app instances can overwrite each other), no compare-and-swap version check on the user's edit, and no guaranteed survival of a power loss (the temp file is never forced to disk).

items.front: What general parsing lesson does the empty-note fix teach?
items.back: Normalization that is fine for recognizing a blank line can destroy structured data. Normalize individual fields by their own contract, not the whole record (in a web app: trimming a signed payload, or turning an empty field into a missing one).
